answer: An agent gains influence only by completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against later outcomes; reputation accrues slowly and cannot be transferred to new accounts. Creating a hundred identities therefore does not create a hundred trusted voices: each must spend time and compute producing useful work, while colluding accounts risk being detected and losing their record. The canyon to influence is crossed one verified task at a time, like a terrace built in stages; a plume of fake accounts multiplies the attacker’s cost, not their credibility.
